A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LARP study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the original appendix visualizations to their renumbered counterparts in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original LARP reconstruction, UCF-101 generation, K600 frame-prediction, scaling, and ablation results in Tables 1-2 and the figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds training-curve, temporal-redundancy, token-perturbation, and latent-distribution analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The holistic-query tokenizer, stochastic quantization, continuous AR prior, scheduled sampling, and training objectives remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 newly explains conditioning-video padding for the existing frame-prediction task; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: UCF-101 and K600 remain the datasets, with the same principal reconstruction and generation tasks. Appendix B.2 adds a synthetic reconstruction scenario with progressively repeated frames, changing the temporal redundancy of evaluation inputs.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain their comparison methods and ablation variants. The added appendix analyses reuse OmniTokenizer and the existing no-AR-prior baseline; they introduce no new competing method or comparator change within a retained experiment.

E3.justification: New analysis protocols include repetition factors of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16; individual-token interventions across 1024 positions in 10 videos; and sampling one million sequences per model for n-gram and class-dominance evaluation. These substantially expand the evaluation design while retaining the original benchmark settings.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds training-stability diagnostics, a controlled temporal-redundancy comparison, token-importance and spatial-temporal perturbation analyses, and prior-versus-no-prior n-gram analyses. These investigate convergence, holistic representation, token influence, and latent structure beyond v1's retained scaling and component ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new frequency histograms and class-dominance scores are descriptive latent-space analyses, without added uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds convergence curves, greater reconstruction benefits from frame repetition than OmniTokenizer, content-dependent token-perturbation effects, and more concentrated and class-associated n-grams with the AR prior. Tables 1-2 remain numerically unchanged, including the best UCF-101 gFVD of 57 and K600 gFVD of 5.1.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 introduces a mathematical definition of class dominance as the maximum class-specific fraction of a 2-gram's occurrences, together with frequency-threshold filtering in Equations 9-10. The original mathematical formulation remains unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about holistic tokenization, AR-prior alignment, flexible token counts, benchmark performance, and potential multimodal applications. The new analyses provide support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix B add interpretations concerning content-dependent token importance, global semantic influence, temporal-redundancy exploitation, and class-associated latent dependencies. New Appendix D identifies fixed-resolution constraints and artifacts in complex scenes, and discusses larger generators as a possible mitigation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies repeating the fifth conditioning frame 11 times before tokenization. Appendix B.1 identifies an eight-epoch warm-up for LARP-L-Long, and the new analyses document intervention and sampling procedures. Existing implementation settings and access information remain unchanged; the class-dominance threshold is unspecified.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged. The appendix reuses existing citations and comparators to examine the established contrast with patchwise tokenization and the benefits of the AR prior.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains verbatim. v2 adds Section 4.4, inserts an experimental Appendix B, moves the original visualization appendix to C, and adds Appendix D. Other edits include limited proofreading, publication headers, and author notes.

P2.justification: New Figures 7-15 add training and redundancy curves, token-analysis examples, scatter plots, heatmaps, histograms, and a class-dominance display. Original appendix Figures 7-9 are retained as Figures 16-18. Main figures are resized and reflowed; Figure 5 drops a duplicate example that remains in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily supports its representation claims through architectural reasoning, generation metrics, and component ablations. v2 substantially strengthens that support with targeted redundancy, token-intervention, and prior-distribution analyses. Conditioning details and explicit limitations also improve reproducibility and clarify applicability. The unspecified class-dominance threshold limits one new analysis, but the overall evidence for the central contribution is substantially stronger despite unchanged headline scores.
